nodes.name: Galvanostatic Electrodeposition of NiM
nodes.procedure: NiM electrocatalysts (M = Cu, Co, Zn, Mo) were prepared by galvanostatic electrodeposition in a standard three-electrode system using iron foam (IF) as the substrate. A high electrodeposition current density of -0.2 A cm^-2 was used to ensure that all Mδ+ was reduced to M. The high negative potential electrodeposition process promotes the construction of a porous structure due to hydrogen bubbles acting as soft templates (see details in the Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Electrochemical Oxidation of NiM
nodes.procedure: The as-deposited NiM surface was oxidized by an electrochemical oxidation process to form partially oxidized NiM (O-NiM), introducing oxygen atoms to create local NiOOH structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu shows diffraction peaks between standard Ni and Cu peaks, shifted toward lower angle with increasing Cu content, indicating NiCu solid solution formation. No clear nickel oxide peaks detected after oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Taking NiCu as an example (Figures 2c and S5), it can be seen that the diffraction peaks are located between the standard Ni and Cu peaks. With the increase in Cu content, the peaks are shifted toward a lower angle ... no clear XRD peaks of nickel oxides were detected.

nodes.characterization_summary: O-NiCu consists of numerous irregular nanoparticles with particle sizes of 20-100 nm uniformly covering iron foam skeleton, surface morphology unchanged after electrochemical oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The O-NiCu sample consists of numerous irregular nanoparticles with particle sizes of 20 - 100 nm, which uniformly cover the entire skeleton of iron foam (Figures 2d-e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Vibrational bands at 486 cm⁻¹ and 554 cm⁻¹ assigned to polarized Eg and A1g modes of NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy was performed to confirm the formation of oxyhydroxide. As shown in Figure S18, vibrational bands at 486 cm⁻¹ and 554 cm⁻¹ are observed, which can be assigned to the polarized Eg and A1g modes of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes of 0.21 nm and 0.18 nm indexed to (111) and (200) planes of metallic Ni; 0.25 nm fringe indicates local NiOOH (110) structure at Ni particle edge; nanointerface observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2g and Figure S20, the marked lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of 0.21 nm and 0.18 nm can be respectively indexed to the (111) and (200) planes of metallic Ni ... the other lattice fringe spacing of 0.25 nm indicates the local NiOOH (110) structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS: Ni⁰ peaks at 852.7 eV (2p3/2) and 869.9 eV (2p1/2), Ni²⁺ at 855.8/873.5 eV; Cu 2p: Cu⁰ at 932.6/952.5 eV; O 1s: lattice oxygen increased from 23% (NiCu) to 36% (O-NiCu); Ni peaks show ~0.2 eV negative shift in NiCu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectra (Figure 3a), the peaks at 852.7 and 869.9 eV separated by ≈17.2 eV ... can be ascribed to the Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 orbitals ... a pair of peaks are located at 855.8 and 873.5 eV corresponding to Ni in the oxide state (Ni²⁺) ... The peaks of Cu 2p1/2 and Cu 2p3/2 are at 932.6 and 952.5 eV ... the intensity of the lattice oxygen is increased from pristine NiCu (23%) to O-NiCu (36%).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES: absorption edges negatively shifted after Cu introduction; O-NiCu edge between Ni and NiO; EXAFS Ni-Ni peak at 2.16 Å slightly longer for NiCu; reduced intensity for O-NiCu indicates lower coordination number.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3e ... after the introduction of Cu, the adsorption edges defined by the half-height approach are negatively shifted compared to Ni metal ... the absorption edge energy of O-NiCu is between the corresponding values of Ni and NiO ... Figure 3f presents the Fourier transform ... The strong FT peak at 2.16 Å corresponds to the Ni-Ni coordination shell of Ni. The Ni-Ni peak of NiCu is slightly longer than that of Ni metal.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl = 294 mF cm⁻² for O-NiCu (vs Ni: 63 mF cm⁻², NiCu: 95 mF cm⁻², O-Ni: 79 mF cm⁻²), indicating higher ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: O-NiCu shows a Cdl of 294 mF cm⁻² (Figure 4e), distinctly larger than those of Ni (63 mF cm⁻²), NiCu (95 mF cm⁻²), and O-Ni (79 mF cm⁻²), suggesting a higher electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of O-NiCu.

nodes.characterization_summary: O-NiCu shows decreased radius of semicircle in Nyquist plots, indicating facilitated charge-transfer process.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EIS measurements show a decreased radius of the semicircle in the Nyquist plots (Figure 4d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Valence band spectra show d-band center shifted downwards with Cu substitution in NiCu; partial oxidation has no obvious effect on NiCu d-band center.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The changes in the d-band center positions ... were monitored by the valence band spectra (VBS) in XPS measurements. As expected, the d-band spectrum is distinctly shifted downwards with the substitution of Cu for Ni, whereas partial oxidation has no obvious effect on the d-band center of NiCu (Figure 3d).
